newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER ON THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER ON THURSDAY.

text.p: Short-term rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer in fairly quiet trade on Thursday but dealers said they expected them to trend slightly up on the back of a rise in annual inflation in March.
Zimbabwe's all-items consumer index rose 2.6 percentage points in March from February, lifting the year-on-year rate to 19.9 percent.

Money market dealers said the Reserve Bank auctioned off Z$100 million worth of treasury bills at 16.02 percent, a slight rise over Wednesday's average yield of 15.95 percent, indicating an upward track by other money rates.
"I think the authorities (central bank) have realised the rates were too low to match current inflation," one dealer said.
Meanwhile on Thursday, NCDs with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 16.75 percent, unchanged from the previous day and sold at 16.35 percent, also unchanged.
Bank bills were at 16.25 and 16 percent (buying and selling) from 16.25 and 15.80 percent while call money edged up to 15.75 percent from 15.50 percent.
Reserve Bank figures showed the market closed short of Z$32.5 million on Wednesday compared with a Z$30 million surplus on Tuesday.
